title: SRE: canary rollout + auto-disable hooks for quantization route toggle on regression
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
We are shipping opt-in quantization profiles with route-level enablement. SRE needs a safe rollout mechanism (canary %) and an automated disable/rollback path when we detect quality or reliability regressions.

This issue covers:
- Canary evaluation semantics for the route-level quantization toggle (per-route percentage gates, stable assignment, and auditability).
- Regression detection signals (5xx, latency, output-format/structured-output failures, and quality regression signals fed from eval harness + online monitors) that can trigger an automatic disable.
- Control plane hooks and runbook-aligned workflow: when auto-disable fires, we must flip the route setting to baseline, record an audit log entry, and emit a clear event/metric for oncall.

Non-goals:
- Designing the route-level config model itself (handled in ENG-18451 / platform docs).
- Building the full dashboard UX (tracked separately; this ticket only ensures the signals exist and are actionable).

Primary objective: ensure we can do a limited beta with canaries and a fast, low-blast-radius rollback mechanism that does not require manual intervention for common regression classes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Canary gate exists and is enforced in request path:
- Route-level setting supports canary percentage (0-100).
- Stable assignment for canary (no per-request random flips that cause inconsistent outputs within a session), based on a deterministic hash of request context (org_id + route_id + optionally conversation_id where available).
- Canary decision is surfaced in logs/trace tags so we can segment metrics.

2) Auto-disable triggers and actions:
- When a regression signal crosses threshold, the system can automatically set the effective route quantization setting to disabled (baseline) for the impacted route (and optionally customer override if signal is customer-scoped).
- Auto-disable action is idempotent, rate-limited, and produces an audit log entry + oncall notification event.

3) Signals available with clear ownership and thresholds:
- Reliability: increase in 5xx rate or incompatibility fallbacks causing elevated error volume.
- Latency: p95 latency regression vs baseline (segmented by route + profile_id).
- Structured output: JSON/schema/tool-calling parse/validation failures increase.
- Quality: external quality regression event ingested from eval harness/monitoring (pass/fail gating) with route mapping.

4) Operational safety:
- Auto-disable cannot flap repeatedly (cooldown window).
- Auto-disable does not break billing attribution (requests continue, tagged baseline after disable).
- Clear manual override exists to re-enable (SRE runbook + audit trail).
implementation_notes:
High-level approach implemented across platform + SRE automation:

A) Canary evaluation
- Implemented in route policy evaluation: if quantization enabled with canary_percent < 100, determine quantized vs baseline deterministically.
- Deterministic hashing key: (org_id, route_id, canonical_request_key). For hosted chat where a conversation_id is present, prefer it to keep consistent behavior over a multi-turn session. Fall back to request_id only when no stable key exists.
- Canary decision is appended to request execution tags: execution_mode in {quantized, baseline}; additionally add quantization_canary=true/false.

B) Regression detector inputs
- Online SLO signals come from metrics tagged by route_id + profile_id + execution_mode (added in telemetry work).
- “Quality regression signal” is treated as an external event that includes: profile_id/version, route_id (or model + org mapping), and severity.

C) Auto-disable mechanism
- A small automation service/worker (existing rollout automation framework) watches regression events and triggers a config write to disable quantization for a route.
- Writes go through the same control plane API as Console/API changes to preserve RBAC + audit logs.
- Cooldown: 30 minutes per route per trigger class; do not re-attempt disable if already disabled.

D) Audit + notifications
- Audit log entry includes: actor=system, action=auto_disable_quantization, route_id, previous_state, new_state, trigger_type, trigger_metric, trigger_window.
- Emit oncall event: quantization.auto_disable.fired with same dimensions; links to dashboard slice for the route.

Notes/edge cases
- If runtime already falls back to baseline due to incompatibility, we do NOT immediately auto-disable solely on fallback_count>0; we require a threshold + window to avoid disabling due to isolated mismatches during rollout. Fallback is still logged with reason.
- For Dedicated/Private: auto-disable is supported only where the customer has enabled the automation integration; otherwise we emit alerts and require manual disable (documented in runbook).
testing_plan:
Unit tests
- Hashing/assignment determinism: same inputs yield same canary decision.
- Canary boundary values: 0/1/99/100.
- Cooldown logic + idempotency.

Integration tests
- Mixed traffic: ensure baseline + quantized requests can coexist and metric tags are correct.
- Auto-disable flow: inject synthetic regression event, verify config write occurs, route becomes baseline, audit log event emitted.

Load tests
- Verify automation does not overload config service during incident conditions (batching + rate limit).

Failure injection
- Control plane write failures: ensure we retry with backoff and alert if unable to disable.
- Partial outages: ensure request path remains safe (baseline default) when policy evaluation fails or config unavailable.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal)
- Enable canary=1% for a single internal route (batch summarization) with int8 profile on supported GPUs.
- Validate audit events and dashboard segmentation.

Phase 1 (beta)
- Allow beta customers to set canary percentages in Console.
- Auto-disable enabled by default for Hosted for the regression classes: 5xx spike, structured-output failures spike. Quality-signal auto-disable enabled for routes that have eval harness coverage.

Phase 2 (GA readiness)
- Expand triggers to latency regression once baselines are stable and we’ve validated noise characteristics.
- Document dedicated/private behavior and customer opt-in for automation integration.
comments: 2026-01-14 (Rafael Mendes): Proposing we reuse rollout automation framework used for model rollouts. It already supports cooldown + audit events; only missing piece is new trigger sources (structured-output failures + eval harness events).

2026-01-16 (Logan Wright): Telemetry tags are required for segmentation (route_id/profile_id/execution_mode). ENG-18472 must land before we can set meaningful thresholds. In the meantime we can wire the control-plane action and test with synthetic events.

2026-01-21 (Mina Haddad): Canary determinism: please don’t key on request_id by default; it will cause per-turn drift. Prefer conversation_id when available; otherwise org_id+route_id+client_user_id (if present) seems better. If none available, document behavior as best-effort.

2026-01-28 (Selene Huang): Auto-disable should initially trigger on clear correctness regressions: JSON parse/validation failures and tool-call schema failures. Latency can be noisy; recommend alert-only until we have more baselines.

2026-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): Oncall requirement: when auto-disable fires, page should include route name, org, trigger, and a direct link to a dashboard view filtered to route+profile. Please ensure event payload has these fields.
2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes): Implemented cooldown=30m + hard cap of 5 disable actions per org per hour to protect config service during cascading failures.
